item.title: Google Says Go Is the Ideal Language for AI Coding — HN Argues Back in 317 Comments
item.description: Google's developer blog called Go the ideal language for AI-assisted engineering; Hacker News answered with 317 comments. Our take: both sides are doing the wrong math. In the AI era you pick a language by verification cost, not writing speed — here is the three-factor ledger, our picks, and an experiment to run tonight

item.title: Rust Officially Sets Rules for AI Coding: LLM-Written PRs Must Ship Tests, Merges Circuit-Break at 50%
item.description: On August 5, 2026, five Rust teams adopted an LLM usage policy for rust-lang/rust: AI-created code can land in the compiler, but only with disclosure, mandatory tests, and a ban on soundness-critical paths — and if LLM PRs exceed 50% of merges in any 6-week window, a circuit breaker halts them. Full policy breakdown and community debate inside

item.title: Qwen3.8-Max Released: 2.4T-Parameter Coding Model, Open Weights Next Week
item.description: Qwen3.8-Max is out: 2.4T total params (95B active), the first Max-class model to open its weights (HF + ModelScope next week). Autonomous coding case: 265 commits in 16 days. PaperBench 93.0 leads all models; SWE-bench Pro still trails Claude Fable 5. Includes Claude Code / Codex setup.

item.title: SOTA on Paper, Engineering Traps in Production: Claude Opus 5's Hidden Risks
item.description: Claude Opus 5 tops Frontier-Bench and CursorBench at half the price of Fable 5. We look past the benchmarks to three engineering traps most teams miss.

item.title: How to Write an AI Skill That Actually Works
item.description: A complete guide to building production-grade AI Skills from scratch. Covers thin-shell routing, progressive disclosure, session discipline, cross-tool compatibility, testing, and knowledge evolution, based on the agentskills.io open standard and real community experience.

item.title: Codex + Superpowers AGENTS.md V3: Finally Working for Real
item.description: From V2 to V3: streamlined task routing, fixed sub-agent deadlock bug, added parallel-first prioritization. Shorter context, better results. Full config included.

item.title: Someone Tested Claude Code 2,430 Times and Discovered Its Tool Selection Logic Isn't What You'd Expect
item.description: Amplifying.ai ran 2,430 tests on Claude Code and found that in 12 out of 20 categories, it prefers writing custom code over using existing tools. GitHub Actions 94%, Stripe 91%, shadcn/ui 90% selection rates are striking, while AWS, GCP, and Azure got zero primary picks.

item.title: GLM-5 Just Dropped: $1/M Tokens Doing What $5/M Does — Is Your AI Subscription Still Worth It?
item.description: Zhipu AI's GLM-5 scores 77.8% on SWE-bench with a 744B MoE architecture, MIT license, and $1/M token pricing — just 3 points behind Claude Opus 4.6 at 1/5 the cost. We ran real benchmarks and code tests to help you decide where your AI budget should go.

item.title: Codex 5.3 Tuning Guide: One AGENTS.md to Run Tasks in Parallel and Cut the Fluff
item.description: Configure GPT-5.3-Codex with collab parallelism to run three projects simultaneously, cutting single-task time from 10 minutes to 3. Includes complete config.toml and AGENTS.md templates, ready to copy.

item.title: Codex CLI Ships 12 Versions in 20 Days: Features That Doubled My Coding Productivity
item.description: From v0.86 to v0.97, how did OpenAI's AI coding assistant transform? This article walks you through the most practical new features across these 12 versions—see which productivity boosters you've been missing.

item.title: 2025 Indie Dev Frugal Stack: Money-Saving AI Coding + Zero-Cost Web Deploy (DeepSeek R1 0528, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3)
item.description: 2025 trends: DeepSeek R1 0528, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3 free/low-cost AI coding combos + zero-cost web deployment with Vercel/Cloudflare Pages/Workers — a practical playbook for indie developers.
